## 1. HUB-GEM-11 · TRIAL 1: Titan's blind coin-photo test, main pack (30 coins)

**Due:** 2026-11-23 · **State:** now

**Why:** TRIAL (do these first, in this order): a measured test of what this model can do; scored against answers or measurements Claude holds, not by opinion. Vision at the level of a coin's mint mark. The same 30 photos and the same prompt every model has taken (results in Titan's collaborators/MODEL_ACCURACY.md); best so far on this pack: core accuracy 85 % (Gemini app, Oct 2026). The bar to do Titan's Phase 2 research is core accuracy 95 %, invented values 1 % or less, false confidence 5 % or less.

**What it unlocks:** If this model clears the bar, it does Titan's Phase 2 coin research (variety and catalogue numbers) instead of only checking facts.

**Read first:**
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1J8GyMMRBMhpMXCZRaaKZf3xemV24gunZ (the same photos and PROMPT.md in Drive, added 2026-11-20 because raw GitHub images did not open in the Gemini app: open each photo here)
- https://github.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/tree/main/docs/bakeoff/pack-20261008-main (the 30 photos, BK-xxxx.webp)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/docs/bakeoff/pack-20261008-main/PROMPT.md (the test's own prompt and answer format: follow it exactly)
- each photo opens at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/main/docs/bakeoff/pack-20261008-main/BK-xxxx.webp

**Do this:**
1. Read PROMPT.md and follow it word for word: it is the same prompt every model got (version BAKEOFF@2026-10-08).
2. Open each of the 30 photos at full size. Read the coin itself: legend, date, value, mint mark, design.
3. Blind means blind: do not open the Titan repository's data, its other photos, or any earlier answer to this test (yours included, in this chat's history or Drive). A looked-up answer scores as invalid. Numista, NGC and PCGS are allowed for the KM number only.
4. Where you are not sure of a field, answer null. A confident wrong answer costs more than a blank.
5. Save the JSON object PROMPT.md asks for; put your exact model name and version (as the app shows it) in the run report.

**Make:** `bakeoff_{yourmodel}_main_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Titan Reliquary/bakeoff (blind photo test)/ (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1njWOHedDNNX3rh3GJ4Pz_L_KyyYeYcH_)

**Shape:** `one JSON object keyed by the 30 file names without .webp, exactly as PROMPT.md shows`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `country` (text): issuing country in English, or null
- `year` (text): Western year of the date on the shown side, or null
- `denom` (text): value and unit as on the coin, or null
- `mint` (text): mint mark letters; "" if the shown side has none; null if you cannot tell
- `km` (text): Krause number without 'KM#', or null
- `confidence` (text): high / med / low for the whole answer

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] All 30 keys, each with the six fields.
- [ ] Every null is a real 'cannot tell', not a skipped photo.
- [ ] Nothing came from the Titan repository's data or an earlier run.
- [ ] Valid JSON, named exactly as asked.

**How many:** 30

**Done when:** All 30 answered and saved.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude scores it with tools/bakeoff/score.py against the sealed key (its sha256 is in tools/bakeoff/commitments.jsonl) and tells you only the totals.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- an answer that matches the record but not the photo (looked up)
- fewer than the count
- not the shape PROMPT.md asks for

## 3. HUB-GEM-10 · Prometheus Hub: the function spec, written as the build plan

**Due:** 2026-11-30 · **State:** now

**SENT BACK, DO IT AGAIN:** Sent back 2026-11-20: hub_gemini_function-spec_20261116-1930.md answers a different template (B-G are 'Who uses it and when, Data shapes, Core flows, Known gaps and bugs, Improvements worth making, Charter compliance', not the eight headings asked), and 5 of its 25 file:line references run past the end of the file (e.g. deck/app.js:1-385 when the file had 322 lines). Write it again from the live code with the eight headings, the counts below, and line numbers you opened.

**Why:** Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.

**What it unlocks:** Joseph goes pillar by pillar, function before form; this file is the plan Claude builds Prometheus Hub from, step by step.

**Read first:**
- https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/./
- https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/deck
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/docs/CHARTER.md (section 16: protections)

**Do this:**
1. Open the live page (https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/./) on a phone-sized browser and use every section.
2. Read the code (https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/deck): every file the page loads, and pillar.json.
3. Write section A from what is there now, with file:line for each item; then B to H.
4. Write for Claude to build from: exact, testable, nothing vague like 'improve the UX'.

**Make:** `hub_gemini_function-spec_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.md`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `one markdown file with exactly these headings, in this order: A What it does today | B What Joseph needs it to do | C Data | D Screens | E Rules and edge cases | F Acceptance tests | G Order of work | H Must not`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `A What it does today` (list): every section, control and number on the live page, each with the file and line in the code that makes it (e.g. app.js:142)
- `B What Joseph needs it to do` (8+ user stories): 'As Joseph, when ..., I want ..., so that ...'; from the pillar's mission and its own data; never invent facts about his life
- `C Data` (table): record | field | type | unit | required | example | storage key (prometheus.<pillar>.<name>) | read by which other pillar
- `D Screens` (per screen): purpose; every element top to bottom; every number with its formula and source field; the empty state text; the error state
- `E Rules and edge cases` (10+): dates and time zones, missing data, offline, two devices, a value of 0 vs unknown
- `F Acceptance tests` (12+): Given / When / Then, each checkable in a phone browser in under two minutes
- `G Order of work` (numbered steps): each step small enough for one build, with what Joseph can use after it
- `H Must not` (list): the charter's protections that apply, no server or account, no made-up numbers

**One finished row, as an example (use your own data, never copy this):**

```
F7. Given an oil change logged at 12,000 mi and a 6,000 mi interval, when the odometer is set to 17,500 mi, then the service card shows 'due in 500 mi' in amber.
```

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every item in A has a file:line that exists.
- [ ] B has 8+ stories and none invents a personal fact.
- [ ] C names every field with type and example.
- [ ] F has 12+ tests, each with one Given, one When, one Then.
- [ ] G steps are in an order that can ship one by one.
- [ ] All eight headings, in order.
- [ ] Every file:line in A is the line that does what the item says, in the code as it is on the day you write (Claude opens 10 at random).

**How many:** 1

**Done when:** 1 file exactly in the shape, every self-check line true.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude opens 10 rows (or 10 claims) at random and compares them with their source.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field
- a row copied from another row with the names changed
- a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
- a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
- a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
- a guess written as a fact (say 'not found' instead)
- anything about Joseph's own accounts, balances, mail or records beyond what the task names
- a file:line past the end of its file, or pointing at code that does something else
- a personal detail (address, names, devices, accounts) that is not in the pillar's own code or data
